reader.title: Attempted lynching at Barnesville, Minnesota
bases: A mob took a jailed man accused of assaulting his wife from the jail, in a report the papers called a 'lynching bee' averted, and one version says it put a rope around his neck to hang him (A1, A2, A3).

A mob seized the accused man from jail to punish him for an alleged assault on his wife, but every report says he was not killed: either the mob let him go (A1) or officers and citizens rescued him unharmed (A2, A3); it was an attempted lynching.

Two apparently independent versions (A1 and the Journal special carried by A2 and A3) agree that a mob took a man jailed for beating or assaulting his wife from the Barnesville jail and that he survived, though they disagree on how he escaped.

summary.text: The attempted lynching at Barnesville, Minnesota, took place in late March 1888, when an armed mob broke into the town jail and carried off a man held on his wife's complaint of assault.
The man, whose name was printed as Polenski, Poliuski and Polanski, survived without harm.
Reports disagree on how he escaped: one says the mob relented when he begged for his life, the other that officers and citizens rescued him.
According to a Barnesville special to the Minneapolis Journal, the man had been arrested for assault on the complaint of his wife and lodged in jail.
The Rock Island Daily Argus described him simply as "a wife beater."
On the night of March 29, an armed mob broke into the jail and carried him off.
In the Journal's account, armed officers, aided by a posse of citizens, rescued him before the mob had harmed him, and a "lynching bee" was "narrowly averted."
The Argus version went further, saying the mob placed a rope around his neck to hang him but let him go after he "begged so piteously for his life," on a promise of good behavior.
No report of arrests of mob members, or of the outcome of the assault charge against the man, appears in the coverage.
The story reached readers outside Minnesota only as a brief item.

On March 31 the Beatrice Daily Express in Nebraska printed the Journal special under a headline about spoiling a lynching bee, and the same day the Argus in Illinois ran its own one-sentence version among its condensed news.
The Brookhaven Leader in Mississippi carried the Journal version on April 5 among its additional dispatches, putting "bee" in quotation marks and dating the event "on the 30th."
None of the reports named the man's race or commented on the mob, and the Argus framed the episode around the prisoner's pleading rather than any intervention by officers.

The two accounts conflict on the ending: the Argus says the mob itself released him after placing a rope around his neck, while the Journal special, dated from Barnesville, says officers and a citizen posse rescued him and mentions no rope.
The Journal special is the more detailed and the only one sent from the town.

accounts.label: Condensed-news item
accounts.gist: The mob took the wife beater from jail and put a rope around his neck to hang him, but relented when he begged for his life and let him go on a promise of good behavior.

framing.detail: The Rock Island Argus ran a one-sentence item identifying the man as 'a wife beater' and describing his begging 'so piteously' that the mob relented, without comment.
The Beatrice Daily Express and Brookhaven Leader carried the Journal special describing a 'lynching bee' (Brookhaven: 'bee' in quotation marks) narrowly averted by armed officers and citizens.
